name: Top Echelon
summary: Recruiting software for agencies and staffing firms: TE Recruit is an ATS and CRM with resume parsing, pipeline management, hotlists and job-board integrations, while TE Network is a split-placement network for sharing roles and candidates with other recruiting firms.
best_for: recruiting agencies and SMB staffing firms that want an applicant tracking system and CRM in one place, especially ones that would actually work split placements with other recruiters
skip_if: you are an in-house talent team hiring for your own company: this is built around agency and split-placement workflows, so you would carry a network you never use
honest_knock: Almost everything people shop for sits in Professional, not Standard: Smart-TE AI, automations, sequences, inbound email sync and API access are all one tier up, so Standard is a competent but plain ATS. The bigger thing to price honestly is that TE Recruit and TE Network are two separate subscriptions. The network is billed per agency on top of your seats, so "Top Echelon" can mean two bills. And taking the network month-to-month adds a $350 one-time startup fee that annual billing waives.

pricing.entry_price_terms: TE Recruit Standard, per seat · per seat per month billed annually
pricing.notes: (2026-09-10, read on their own pricing page, both billing toggles; re-verified unchanged on 2026-10-06) TE Recruit (the ATS and CRM) runs $79 per seat per month billed annually or $95 month-to-month on Standard, and $95 billed annually or $115 month-to-month on Professional. Those seat rates rose during 2026: the same cards read $75/$89 on Standard and $89/$110 on Professional when we read them on 25 August 2026. TE Network, the split-placement network, is priced per agency rather than per seat and is unchanged: $135 per month billed annually with the $350 startup fee waived, or $150 per month billed monthly plus a $350 one-time startup fee.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 31 October 2026 on the 30-day trial of TE Recruit: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We added two made-up people by hand, attached a file to one, and exported both to a spreadsheet.
findings: The trial showed 30 days, with no card. The account came pre-filled with 100 sample people and 50 sample companies.
The contact importer only continues if you confirm that every imported email address has agreed to receive your emails; we did not tick that, so we added the people by hand.
The export runs in the background, raises a notification and waits on the Files & Exports page; the download needs no email.
The CSV has a header row and kept the names with accents, the multi-line memo and Top Echelon's own ID for each person.
Every exported person had Country set to 'United States of America', although we entered no country; times were in US time.
The attachment downloaded byte-for-byte identical, but attachments are not part of the spreadsheet export.
not_tested: Prices and paying for a plan
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
